findings.evidence: Line 856: `include_build_tier = a.build or a.wine or any(x == "suite:build-check" for x in target_ids)` and line 859: `include_wine = a.wine or any(x.startswith("wine:") for x in target_ids)`, both evaluated before discover() and wine_plan(). Positional filters are only merged into target_ids later, at lines 864-868 (`target_ids.update(pos_exact)`), after the tier and wine decisions were already made. So `run_tests.py suite:build-check` or `run_tests.py wine:<smoke>` never includes the build tier or the wine plan, the filter at 871-872 then matches nothing, and the run exits 0 (see f2).
findings.suggested_investigation: Run `python3 scripts/run_tests.py --list suite:build-check` and `python3 scripts/run_tests.py --list wine:<name>` (with a real smoke name from harness/smokes.toml) and confirm the build/wine items are absent. Then move the pos_exact computation ahead of the include_build_tier/include_wine decisions, or fold positional IDs into target_ids before line 856, and re-check.
findings.why_it_matters: The positional form documented in the help text (`e.g. suite:check-hook-bytes`) silently fails to run tier="build" suites or Wine smokes that the user explicitly named. A gate the user asked for is skipped with no FAIL/ERROR, which weakens the gate.

findings.evidence: Line 871-872: `if target_ids: items = [i for i in items if i.id in target_ids]`. No check that any item survived. The result counts at 982-984 and the return at 995 (`return 1 if counts["FAIL"] or counts["ERROR"] else 0`) do not count an empty selection as a failure. An `--id` typo, an `--ids-file` with stale ids, or a positional that matches nothing therefore produces `0 passed, 0 failed` and exit code 0.
findings.suggested_investigation: Run `python3 scripts/run_tests.py --id cpp:does_not_exist; echo $?` and confirm exit 0 with zero items. Fix by returning non-zero (or an ERROR result) when a requested id/filter selects no items, and check that the same holds for the pre-existing `-k` path.
findings.why_it_matters: A test-selection mistake reads as a green gate. Callers that rely on the exit code (the Gate Invariant requires a hard stop on failure) can be told that tests passed when none ran.

findings.evidence: Line 620-621: `except Exception:\n        pass` around the manifest lookup, then line 622-626: `for d in (REPO / "patch_manager_mods").iterdir(): ... clean = d.name.replace("_src", "")...; if clean and (clean in stem or stem in clean): return d`. The substring match is order-dependent (iterdir order is filesystem-defined) and a short cleaned name such as a 2-3 letter directory can match an unrelated kpatch stem. The `_extract_dll` path (line 671-675) then builds and copies whichever DLL this returns.
findings.suggested_investigation: Check the directory names under patch_manager_mods/ for short names that are substrings of other kpatch stems. Then call resolve_mod_for_smoke with a kpatch whose stem is a real mod name and one that matches two dirs, and see which dir comes back. Also temporarily break the `_static_common` import and see whether resolution changes. Prefer failing with RuntimeError over the substring fallback unless the match is unique.
findings.why_it_matters: With `dll_from = "build"`, a Wine smoke can be fed a DLL from a different mod and report PASS. The broad except also hides a failing `_static_common` import, which silently pushes resolution onto the fuzzy path.

findings.evidence: Line 641-655: rebuild_needed is decided only by mtimes of files with suffix in (".cpp", ".h", ".hpp", ".inc", ".def") under mod_dir and _shared_src, compared against `dll_candidates[0]` only. Line 639 and 662 glob `*/build/*.dll` and take the first hit. Changes to tests/include headers, build flags, CMake/Makefile or other suffixes, or a newer build of a different candidate, do not trigger a rebuild.
findings.suggested_investigation: Touch tests/include/SafeRead.h (or another include used by the harness) with a newer mtime than the cached DLL, run `--wine --dll-from build` on one smoke, and check whether build_check --keep is re-invoked. Also check whether the glob can return more than one DLL under build/<key>/*/build/.
findings.why_it_matters: A cached build DLL can be stale. `smoke_build` then tests and reports PASS against a binary that does not match the current sources, which is a gate that can pass on the wrong code.

findings.evidence: Line 798-799: `ap.add_argument("--json", nargs="?", const="-", default=None, ...)` alongside line 806: `ap.add_argument("filters", nargs="*", ...)`. And lines 983-994: the human summary line (983-984) is printed to stdout first, then `if a.json == "-": print(out_str)` writes the JSON to the same stdout.
findings.suggested_investigation: Run `python3 scripts/run_tests.py --json --list` and `python3 scripts/run_tests.py --json suite:check-hook-bytes` and inspect the output and any files created in the cwd. Consider putting the summary on stderr when `--json -` is used.
findings.why_it_matters: `run_tests.py --json suite:x` makes argparse consume `suite:x` as the JSON output path, so the filter is dropped and a file is written. `--json` alone with no path prints the summary text and the JSON together on stdout, which is not parseable as JSON by consumers.

notes: Checked the callee build_check.py by grep: it stages copies only under the TMP build directory (shutil.rmtree/copy2 within key_dir) and does not reference the Steam/game directory, so `_ensure_built_dll` does not reach an install path. The `MASTER_LEDGER_TEST=1` global env set at run_tests.py:68 matches the same pattern in scripts/test_plan_manager.py:16 and is consistent with scripts/master_ledger.py:77, so it is not reported. The `RuntimeError` -> FAIL reclassification in smoke_build (line 710-711) is a judgement call, not a gate weakening, and is not reported. No secrets or credential paths were accessed.
